command_applicability.command_recommendation: After decision, use verified stable IDs with a valid RAID5 count/path; capture healthy sync, single-member degraded availability/hash, rebuild progress/thermal load, clean state and separately approved cleanup.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a stable-identity RAID5 state machine with parity sync, one-member degrade, continued hash/I/O, monitored rebuild and controlled cleanup.

modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Execution waits for authoritative level/count rather than silently substituting invalid topology.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RAID5 tolerates one member failure; a second failure or latent read error during rebuild can lose the array.

review_improvement: Rejects invalid RAID5 topology and binds parity/degraded/rebuild coverage to exact disposable media with second-fault and cleanup controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: RAID5 needs at least three members because one member's worth of distributed parity protects against a single failure. A two-device command cannot form the intended topology, and during rebuild redundancy is exhausted; therefore member count and one-fault-only guards are safety-critical, not optional parameters.
